questions.q: A solution that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration is called an ______ solution.
questions.e: In an ideal solution ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0; n-hexane and n-heptane form a nearly ideal solution.

questions.q: Scuba divers can suffer from 'the bends' because the solubility in blood of which gas changes with pressure?
questions.e: At depth, high pressure dissolves more nitrogen in the blood (Henry's law). Rising quickly releases it as bubbles in the blood.

questions.q: 10 g of glucose is dissolved in 90 g of water. What is the mass percentage of glucose?
Two solutions that have the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature are called ______ solutions.
questions.e: Red blood cells are isotonic with 0.9% NaCl (normal saline), so they neither swell nor shrink in it.

questions.q: What is the van't Hoff factor for K2SO4 in a dilute aqueous solution, assuming complete dissociation?
questions.e: K2SO4 → 2K+ + SO4^2-, giving 3 ions per formula unit.

questions.q: 5.85 g of NaCl (molar mass 58.5 g/mol) is dissolved to make 500 mL of solution. What is its molarity?
The vapour pressure of pure benzene is 640 mm Hg. A non-volatile solute lowers it to 600 mm Hg. What is the mole fraction of the solute?
questions.e: Relative lowering of vapour pressure = mole fraction of solute = (640 − 600)/640 = 0.0625.

questions.q: 0.1 mol of urea (a non-electrolyte) is dissolved in 500 g of water (Kf = 1.86 K kg/mol, Kb = 0.52 K kg/mol).
p: (a) What is the molality of the solution?
(b) What is the depression in freezing point?
(c) What is the elevation in boiling point?

questions.q: In an electrolytic cell, reduction takes place at the ______.
questions.e: Reduction always takes place at the cathode and oxidation at the anode, in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

questions.q: The reciprocal of resistance is called ______.
questions.e: Conductance G = 1/R, measured in siemens (S).

questions.q: How does the molar conductivity of an electrolyte solution change on dilution?
questions.e: On dilution the volume containing one mole of electrolyte increases (and, for weak electrolytes, ionisation increases), so Λm increases.

questions.q: The rusting of iron needs both oxygen and ______.
questions.e: Rusting is an electrochemical process: iron is oxidised at anodic spots and oxygen is reduced in the presence of water.

questions.q: E°(Ag+/Ag) = +0.80 V and E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V. Find E°cell for Cu + 2Ag+ → Cu2+ + 2Ag.
questions.e: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.80 − 0.34 = 0.46 V. (Doubling the Ag half-reaction does not change E°.)

questions.q: How many faradays of charge are needed to produce 1 mol of Cl2 at the anode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl?
questions.e: 2Cl- → Cl2 + 2e-, so 1 mol of Cl2 needs 2 mol of electrons, which is 2 F.

questions.q: A conductivity cell has a cell constant of 1.29 cm^-1. A solution in it has a resistance of 100 Ω. What is its conductivity?
questions.e: κ = cell constant/R = 1.29/100 = 0.0129 S cm^-1.

questions.q: For the cell Zn | Zn2+ (0.1 M) || Cu2+ (1 M) | Cu at 298 K, E°cell = 1.10 V and n = 2. Use Ecell = E°cell − (0.059/n) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]).
p: (a) What is the value of log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])?
questions.e: log(0.1/1) = −1. Ecell = 1.10 − (0.059/2)(−1) = 1.10 + 0.0295 = 1.13 V. Zinc is oxidised, so it is the anode.

questions.q: As a reaction proceeds, its rate usually ______ because the concentrations of the reactants fall.
questions.e: Rate depends on reactant concentration (except in zero-order reactions), so it slows down as reactants are used up.

questions.q: In the Arrhenius equation k = A e^(−Ea/RT), A is called the pre-exponential or ______ factor.
questions.e: A, the frequency factor, is related to how often molecules collide in the correct orientation.

questions.q: What is the unit of the rate constant of a zero-order reaction?
questions.e: For zero order, rate = k, so k has the same unit as rate: mol L^-1 s^-1. (s^-1 is first order and L mol^-1 s^-1 is second order.)

questions.q: The hydrolysis of an ester in a large excess of water follows first-order kinetics although two molecules react. Such reactions are called ______ reactions.
questions.e: Water is in such excess that its concentration hardly changes, so the rate depends only on the ester.

questions.q: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 20 min. What is its rate constant?
About how many half-lives does a first-order reaction take to be 99.9% complete? (Nearest whole number.)
questions.e: After n half-lives the fraction left is (1/2)^n. (1/2)^10 = 1/1024 ≈ 0.001, which is 0.1% left.

questions.q: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. Find Ea using log(k2/k1) = (Ea/2.303R) × (T2 − T1)/(T1T2), with R = 8.314 J K^-1 mol^-1. (One decimal place.)
For 2N2O5 → 4NO2 + O2, N2O5 disappears at a rate of 0.02 mol L^-1 s^-1.
p: (a) At what rate is NO2 formed?
(b) At what rate is O2 formed?
(c) What is the rate of the reaction, −(1/2) d[N2O5]/dt?
questions.e: Rate = −(1/2) d[N2O5]/dt = (1/4) d[NO2]/dt = d[O2]/dt = 0.01 mol L^-1 s^-1. So NO2 forms at 4 × 0.01 = 0.04 and O2 at 0.01 mol L^-1 s^-1.

questions.q: Which transition metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.e: Mercury (melting point −39 °C) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: An alloy of about 95% lanthanoid metals with iron, used in lighter flints, is called ______.
questions.e: Mischmetal sparks when struck, so it is used in lighter flints and in magnesium-based alloys for bullets and shells.

questions.q: In making KMnO4, MnO2 is fused with KOH and an oxidising agent such as KNO3. What dark green compound is formed first?
questions.e: 2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O. The green manganate is then oxidised to purple permanganate.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons does the Cu2+ ion have (Z of Cu = 29)?
questions.e: Cu2+ is [Ar] 3d9: nine d electrons leave one unpaired electron.

questions.q: Transition metals form interstitial compounds when small atoms such as H, C or N are trapped in the holes of their crystal ______.
questions.e: Examples are TiC, Mn4N and Fe3H. These compounds are hard and have high melting points.

questions.q: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of the Cr3+ ion (Z of Cr = 24).
questions.e: Cr3+ is [Ar] 3d3 with 3 unpaired electrons: μ = √(n(n + 2)) = √15 = 3.87 BM.

questions.q: Cu+ disproportionates into Cu2+ and Cu in water because Cu2+(aq) has a much more negative hydration ______.
questions.e: The large hydration enthalpy of the small, highly charged Cu2+ ion more than makes up for the second ionisation enthalpy of copper.

questions.q: Consider the permanganate ion, MnO4- (Z of Mn = 25).
p: (a) What is the oxidation state of manganese?
(b) How many d electrons does the manganese have in this ion?
(c) Its intense purple colour is not due to d–d transitions but to charge ______.
questions.e: x + 4(−2) = −1 gives x = +7. Mn(+7) is [Ar] 3d0, so no d–d transition is possible; the colour comes from ligand-to-metal charge transfer.

questions.q: The theory of primary and secondary valences of coordination compounds was proposed by ______.
questions.e: Alfred Werner proposed it in 1898 and received the Nobel Prize in 1913.

questions.q: In [Cu(NH3)4]SO4, the part written inside the square brackets is called the coordination ______.
questions.e: The central metal with its attached ligands is the coordination entity (or sphere); SO4^2- is the counter ion.

questions.q: What is the coordination number of platinum in [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]?
questions.e: Two NH3 and two Cl- ligands, each monodentate, give 4 donor atoms.

questions.q: What is the oxidation state of platinum in [PtCl6]2-?
[Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 and [Co(NH3)5(SO4)]Br show ______ isomerism.
questions.e: The two compounds give different ions in solution (SO4^2- in one, Br- in the other), so they are ionisation isomers.

questions.q: [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]Cl2 and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]Cl2 show ______ isomerism.
questions.e: The ambidentate NO2- ligand binds through N (nitro) in one and through O (nitrito) in the other.

questions.q: How many geometrical isomers does the square planar complex [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] have?
questions.e: The two Cl- ligands can be next to each other (cis) or opposite each other (trans).

questions.q: Consider [Fe(CN)6]3-, a low-spin octahedral complex (Z of Fe = 26).
p: (a) What is the oxidation state of iron?
(b) How many unpaired electrons does it have?
(c) What is the hybridisation of iron?
questions.e: x + 6(−1) = −3 gives Fe(+3), d5. CN- is a strong-field ligand, so the five electrons pair up in the t2g set (t2g^5), leaving 1 unpaired. Two empty 3d orbitals are used: d2sp3.

questions.q: Chloroform is the common name of ______.
questions.e: Chloroform is CHCl3, trichloromethane. It was once used as an anaesthetic.

questions.q: The non-biodegradable insecticide p,p′-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane is commonly known as ______.
questions.e: DDT was widely used against malaria mosquitoes but is now restricted because it builds up in food chains.

questions.q: Which has the highest boiling point: CH3Cl, CH3Br or CH3I?
questions.e: Boiling point rises with molecular mass and size, because van der Waals forces get stronger: CH3Cl < CH3Br < CH3I.

questions.q: Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes in nucleophilic substitution because the C–X bond gets partial double-bond character through ______.
questions.e: A lone pair on the halogen is delocalised into the ring, which strengthens and shortens the C–X bond.

questions.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (freons) released into the air damage the ______ layer.
questions.e: In the stratosphere, UV light splits CFCs into chlorine radicals, which break down ozone in a chain reaction.

questions.q: Which reacts most readily with aqueous NaOH by nucleophilic substitution?
questions.e: Nitro groups at the ortho and para positions withdraw electrons and stabilise the intermediate carbanion, so 1-chloro-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene reacts even with warm water.

questions.q: An alkyl halide reacts with KCN to give mainly a ______, but with AgCN it gives mainly an isocyanide.
questions.e: KCN is ionic, so CN- attacks through carbon and gives a nitrile. AgCN is mainly covalent, so it attacks through nitrogen and gives an isocyanide.

questions.q: 2-Chlorobutane is CH3CHClCH2CH3.
p: (a) How many chiral carbon atoms does it have?
(b) How many optical isomers (enantiomers) are possible?
(c) With aqueous KOH it gives which alcohol?
questions.e: C2 carries four different groups (H, Cl, CH3 and C2H5), so it is chiral and the compound has 2 enantiomers. Substitution of Cl by OH gives butan-2-ol.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of glycerol, HOCH2–CH(OH)–CH2OH?
questions.e: Glycerol has three carbons with an –OH group on each: propane-1,2,3-triol.

questions.q: In making ethanol by fermenting molasses, the enzymes invertase and ______ are used.
questions.e: Invertase turns sucrose into glucose and fructose; zymase then turns these into ethanol and CO2.

questions.q: A primary alcohol is oxidised by acidified K2Cr2O7 (a strong oxidising agent) to a ______.
questions.e: The aldehyde formed first is oxidised further to the carboxylic acid; PCC is used to stop at the aldehyde.

questions.q: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ______.
questions.e: For example, propan-2-ol is oxidised to propanone.

questions.q: The –OCH3 group of anisole directs incoming electrophiles to the ortho and ______ positions.
questions.e: The lone pairs on oxygen raise the electron density at the ortho and para positions through resonance.

questions.q: Which is the stronger acid: phenol or 2-methylphenol (o-cresol)?
questions.e: The methyl group releases electrons, which destabilises the phenoxide ion, so o-cresol is a weaker acid than phenol.

questions.q: The acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol to ethene goes through which kind of intermediate?
questions.e: The protonated alcohol loses water to give a carbocation, which then loses H+ to give the alkene.

questions.q: Answer the following about phenol, C6H5OH (molar mass 94 g/mol).
p: (a) Phenol reacts with sodium metal to give sodium phenoxide and which gas?
(b) With dilute HNO3 at 298 K it gives ortho- and para-______.
(c) How many grams of phenol give 1 mol of 2,4,6-tribromophenol with excess bromine water?
questions.e: 2C6H5OH + 2Na → 2C6H5ONa + H2. Dilute HNO3 gives a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol. 1 mol of phenol (94 g) gives 1 mol of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of acetaldehyde, CH3CHO?
questions.e: CH3CHO has two carbons and an aldehyde group, so it is ethanal.

questions.q: The common name of methanoic acid is ______ acid.
questions.e: Methanoic acid, HCOOH, was first obtained from red ants (Latin formica, ant).

questions.q: Aldehydes and ketones react with hydroxylamine, NH2OH, to give ______.
questions.e: The carbonyl compound condenses with NH2OH, losing water, to give >C=N–OH, an oxime.

questions.q: Carboxylic acids react with alcohols in the presence of conc. H2SO4 to give ______.
questions.e: This is esterification; for example ethanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate.

questions.q: The Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction halogenates a carboxylic acid at the ______ carbon.
questions.e: With Cl2 or Br2 and red phosphorus, an α-hydrogen is replaced by a halogen.

questions.q: Sodium ethanoate is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO). Which gas is formed?
questions.e: Decarboxylation removes CO2: CH3COONa + NaOH → CH4 + Na2CO3.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde does not undergo aldol condensation because it has no ______ hydrogen.
questions.e: Aldol reactions need an α-hydrogen to form the carbanion; benzaldehyde has none, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction instead.

questions.q: Compound A, C2H4O, reduces Tollens' reagent and gives a positive iodoform test.
p: (b) Which acid is formed when A is oxidised?
(c) Which alcohol is formed when A is reduced with NaBH4?
questions.e: Reducing Tollens' reagent shows an aldehyde, and the iodoform test shows a CH3CO– group, so A is ethanal, CH3CHO. It is oxidised to ethanoic acid and reduced to ethanol.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3NH2?
questions.e: One carbon with an –NH2 group: methanamine (common name methylamine).

questions.q: Amines act as Lewis bases because of the lone pair of electrons on the ______ atom.
questions.e: The nitrogen lone pair can be donated to a proton or a Lewis acid.

questions.q: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia because alkyl groups have an electron-______ (+I) effect.
questions.e: Alkyl groups push electron density onto nitrogen, making its lone pair more available.

questions.q: Ethanenitrile, CH3CN, is reduced with LiAlH4. Which amine is formed?
questions.e: CH3C≡N + 4[H] → CH3CH2NH2. The carbon of the CN group stays in the chain.

questions.q: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to give alcohols with the release of which gas?
questions.e: RNH2 + HNO2 → ROH + N2 + H2O; the brisk effervescence of N2 is a test for primary aliphatic amines.

questions.q: Which class of amines does not react with Hinsberg's reagent?
questions.e: Tertiary amines have no N–H hydrogen, so they cannot form a sulphonamide with benzenesulphonyl chloride.

questions.q: Aniline does not undergo the Friedel–Crafts reaction because it forms a salt with the catalyst ______.
questions.e: The basic –NH2 group gives its lone pair to the Lewis acid AlCl3; the positive nitrogen then deactivates the ring.

questions.q: Aniline is shaken with bromine water at room temperature.
p: (a) How many bromine atoms enter the benzene ring?
(c) Is the –NH2 group ortho/para-directing or meta-directing?
questions.e: The strongly activating –NH2 group directs bromine to both ortho positions and the para position at once, giving a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

questions.q: Proteins are polymers of ______.
questions.a: amino acids|α-amino acids|amino acid|alpha amino acids
questions.e: α-Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds to form proteins.

questions.q: Biological catalysts, which are almost all proteins, are called ______.
questions.e: Enzymes such as maltase and pepsin speed up reactions in living cells.

questions.q: Vitamins A, D, E and K are ______-soluble.
questions.e: They dissolve in fats and are stored in the liver and fatty tissue; vitamins B and C are water-soluble.

questions.q: The sugar present in milk is ______.
questions.e: Lactose is a disaccharide of β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose.

questions.q: Maltose on hydrolysis gives two molecules of ______.
questions.e: Maltose is made of two α-D-glucose units joined by a C1–C4 glycosidic link.

questions.q: Sucrose does not reduce Fehling's solution. Is it a reducing or a non-reducing sugar?
questions.e: In sucrose the reducing groups of glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are used in the glycosidic bond, so it is non-reducing.

questions.q: Cellulose is a straight-chain polysaccharide made of ______-D-glucose units.
questions.e: Cellulose is made of β-D-glucose units joined by C1–C4 glycosidic links; starch is made of α-D-glucose.

questions.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 30% of the bases are adenine.
p: (a) What percentage of the bases are thymine?
questions.e: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C, so T = A = 30%. The remaining 40% is split equally: G = C = 20%.
